A declaration draws as its kind, its id, what it is, and its properties. One carrying a value of a type that says which of its properties holds the kind is headed by what that property holds instead, and the property that type says is its prose reads as the line under that heading. An enum draws the one type it is based on and every value it lists, each with its own id and what that id stands for. A choice draws the types it is one of. A property is a name and a type, and a property holding many draws the collection it is and what that collection holds.

◆

This document declares it. The filled mark and the teal chip say so, and no word is needed because this is what most references are.

A SCOPE
A scope this document reaches declares it, and the chip names that scope. A document reaches a scope by bringing it in, and reaches the language it is written in without. The mark is a diamond within a diamond, because the name is reached rather than written here.

UNDECLARED
Neither this document nor any scope it reaches declares it, so nothing here says what it is. The mark is hollow and the chip is amber.
